youtube.title: How Do Octopuses Find Food in the Dark? | Toxic Tales
youtube.description:
How does an octopus find food without visible light? In dark laboratory flumes, East Pacific red octopuses favored baited stations when approaching upstream. In a separate task, 31 of 41 successful approaches by five analyzed males arrived from inside the estimated chemical plume. These are repeated feeding events, not 41 animals. Suckers might help guide the search, but the experiment did not isolate the sensory organs. Small samples, excluded animals and a proxy plume limit generalization.

Weertman et al. (2025), PLOS ONE. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0330262
Full text: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12507230/
Evidence and credits: https://akshaymohan16.github.io/toxic-tales-library/sources/tt-012.html
Photo: Will Sides, CC BY 4.0 (species reference only): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Octopus_rubescens_189172764.jpg
Licence: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Original conceptual animation, not recorded experiment footage; synthetic neural narration and captions.
